key_insight: Medical VLMs can sound confident, but their full end-to-end predictions often underuse strong vision encoders; in dermatology, the encoder alone outperforms the complete model by about 10.26 percentage points.
clinical_relevance: Better prompting and lightweight reranking may improve image-grounded dermatology decision support without retraining the entire model, but gains in one task can reduce broader medical QA performance.
method: Compared MedSigLIP encoder vs MedGemma end-to-end performance in dermatology.
Tested three hypotheses for weak vision use, including attention analysis and describe-then-decide prompting.
Combined label-free prompting with low-label encoder-assisted reranking while freezing the VLM.
evidence_signal: Across five VLM backbones in dermatology, describe-then-decide raised vision attention by 30–40% and task-specific fine-tuning improved classification but weakened cross-domain medical QA.
watch_item: Results are strongest in dermatology, so generalizing the approach to other medical modalities may require careful validation and attention to tradeoffs between specialization and broader reasoning.
paper_title: How Medical VLMs Underutilize Their Vision Encoders: A Dermatology Perspective
